name: Structured Denoising Diffusion Models in Discrete State-Spaces (SEDD)
problem: Diffusion models were defined in continuous Euclidean space, where adding Gaussian noise and denoising is well defined; text lives in a discrete state space, so naively applying diffusion to tokens is ill-posed.
mechanism: Defines absorbing-state discrete diffusion where the forward process replaces each token with the special MASK token with probability increasing to 1 as t grows, giving a clean absorbing state; and a uniform-state variant where tokens are replaced by uniformly random tokens. The generative model is expressed as an absorbing diffusion that scores the denoising log-ratio, and crucially the paper derives the ELBO and parameterisations for both a 'score entropy' (denoising cross-entropy) objective and the denoising score matching objective, showing that one of these is asymptotically consistent for likelihood while the other is not. The practical consequences are (a) a training objective that actually optimises likelihood, which earlier discrete-diffusion text work lacked, and (b) flexible transition matrices allowing absorbing, uniform, and general time-dependent kernels within one framework. Generation runs T mask-predictor forward passes over the full length-L sequence, so FLOP count is set by T as in any masked diffusion LM; the paper shows sample quality is competitive with AR models at controlled compute, with T chosen per-sample.
speedup_reported: Reports competitive likelihood and sample quality against autoregressive baselines, and introduces annealed / self-conditioned sampling to reduce the number of denoising steps needed. No decoding throughput speedup ratio is published. The paper's contribution is likelihood-correctness of the training objective, not serving throughput, so there is no speedup number to record with baseline and settings.
notes:
ICML 2024 per the arXiv comment field; no journal-ref on the abs page. Method is abbreviated SEDD. This is the theoretical grounding for masked diffusion LMs: LLaDA and most 2025 masked diffusion models are absorbing-state diffusion in this sense, so when someone says a diffusion LM is 'SEDD-style' they mean exactly this transition kernel. The lint engine adoptions are indirect: SEDD's own code was absorbed into the diffusion ecosystem that llama.cpp and vLLM now serve, but SEDD itself is not a released model. Worth recording because it is the paper that established that discrete diffusion can optimise likelihood at all.
